claims.text: Advanced processing routes such as rapid solidification or additive manufacturing with optimized post-annealing can refine alloy microstructure.
Microstructural refinement can reduce magnetic hysteresis in magnetocaloric alloys.
Microstructural refinement can enhance magnetocaloric entropy change under moderate magnetic fields.
Conventionally processed La(Fe,Si)13 or Gd-based magnetocaloric alloys may exhibit relatively coarse grains and irregular phase distributions.
Advanced processing can produce finer and more uniform grain sizes.
Advanced processing can control the distribution of magnetic phases.
Moderate magnetic fields near room temperature are typical operating conditions for magnetocaloric cooling applications.
The optimized processing route establishes a refined microstructure with uniform grain size.
The optimized processing route establishes well-aligned magnetic domains.
A controlled microstructural architecture reduces energy losses caused by magnetic hysteresis.
A controlled microstructural architecture improves magnetic-domain alignment under an applied field.
Reduced hysteresis and improved domain alignment increase the isothermal entropy change during a magnetocaloric cycle.
Reduced hysteresis and improved domain alignment increase the adiabatic temperature change during a magnetocaloric cycle.
The advanced-processed alloy is expected to have a larger isothermal entropy change than the same conventionally processed alloy.
The advanced-processed alloy is expected to have lower hysteresis losses than the same conventionally processed alloy.
Traditional melting and casting produce larger and less-controlled grain structures in magnetocaloric materials.
Unintended phase segregation caused by unsuitable processing parameters may adversely affect magnetocaloric performance.
The magnitude and industrial scalability of the proposed improvement require systematic experimental validation.
